information_boundary: Only HB task/request/registry, admitted source artifacts, TASK_RUBRIC.md, the supplied common base skill and linked interface, and these four output files were consulted. No external literature, target statistics, participants, other author bundles or project history were used.

source_selection.population: NHANES 2001-2004, n=3270, age>=25, no self-reported diagnosed diabetes, FPG<126 mg/dL, available A1c; FOS n=2473 is a separate predominantly white community cohort with medication/FPG-based exclusion and OGTT information.
source_selection.measurement: DCCT-standardized HPLC A1c in percent; fasting plasma glucose with hexokinase assay. NHANES plasma versus task serum is a transfer issue.
source_selection.weighting: NHANES incorporates differential selection probabilities and complex-survey design, unlike target equal-cell WLS.

claims.locator: Results, paragraph beginning 'There was no difference in BMI'; Statistical analysis / NHANES
claims.reported: NHANES age coefficient 0.010 A1c percentage points/year after adjustment for sex, BMI and FPG, P<0.001. FOS 0.012/year additionally considers 2-h postload glucose.
claims.uncertainty: P<0.001; numeric SE/CI for the adjusted coefficient is not reported in the admitted main-text passage. The mentioned online appendix was not fetched.
claims.use: Use NHANES 0.010/year as a fixed conditional H age parameter; 0.10 per decade is unit rescaling. Not the unadjusted 0.014 FOS coefficient or its longitudinal rate. Transfer to Mexico and ages 25-79 is assumed.

claims.reported: NHANES BMI 28.01 +/- 0.14 kg/m^2; text labels descriptive summaries mean +/- SD despite very small quoted dispersions.
claims.uncertainty: The 0.14 is not adopted as individual dispersion, and is not reclassified or converted to an SD. Weighted complex-survey sampling precludes a naive SE*sqrt(n) conversion.
claims.use: 28.01 anchors the untruncated arithmetic BMI mean. Log SD 0.20 is an assumption. Results report no BMI differences across age categories; this supports considering, but does not prove, an age-independent construction.

claims.locator: Table 1 (XML id t1), NHANES nondiabetic columns
claims.reported: Age<40: mean 5.20%, SE 0.01, 97.5th percentile 5.7%; 50-54: mean 5.40%, SE 0.02, 97.5th percentile 6.0%; >=70: mean 5.51%, SE 0.02, 97.5th percentile 6.2%.
claims.estimator: Survey-weighted age-group means/SEs and weighted 97.5th percentiles, not regression intercepts or residual SDs.
claims.use: Qualitative scale and increasing-dispersion anchors for assumed conditional location 5.38 and SD 0.31 at age50 plus 0.001/year. No exact conversion from percentile gaps or SEs to residual SD and no claim of reproducing these three margins.

claims.locator: Results, paragraph beginning 'To determine whether FPG'
claims.reported: Approximately 8 mg/dL increase in FPG across age in both nondiabetic cohorts.
claims.uncertainty: Approximate contrast; explicit age endpoints and sampling uncertainty are not supplied in this main-text statement.
claims.use: Motivates a modest positive glucose-age location slope. 0.16 mg/dL/year is a chosen assumption, not an extracted age-adjusted coefficient.

source_selection.declined: No conversion of FOS/NHANES mean SEs to individual SD, no pooling of different assays/cohorts, no use of the FOS longitudinal change as a cross-sectional slope, and no exact source quantile fit.

source_selection.supplement_selection: Use continuous-BMI rows of Tables S1/S2 from the tabular text extraction; cross-read the page-text extraction of the same supplement. These are two representations of one source, not independent estimates. Supplement JSON structure was inspected but is not the selected numeric representation.
source_selection.population: General Finnish population comparator n=653 from six cities, Health 2011; age30-64. Diabetes excluded using registers, self-reported physician diagnosis, medication, HbA1c>=6.5%, or fasting glucose>=7.0 mmol/L; complete data; fasting4-17h. Russian n293, Somali n184 and Kurdish n275 are comparator groups, not Mexican observations.
source_selection.measurement: General-population glucose measured in serum in mmol/L; migrants in fluoride citrate plasma; HbA1c immunoturbidimetric assay in percent and mmol/mol; objectively measured standing anthropometry.
source_selection.weighting: Stratified sampling, finite population correction and inverse-probability nonresponse weights. Article says all analyses age-adjusted and glucose analyses fasting-time-adjusted. S1 prints age category, sex and BMI coefficients but does not display a fasting-time coefficient.

claims.locator: Supplement Table S1, General population, Age+sex+BMI model, BMI and men rows
claims.reported: BMI beta 0.0240 mmol/L per kg/m^2, P<0.0001; men versus women beta 0.2472 mmol/L, P<0.0001; younger30-44 versus45-64 beta -0.1985 mmol/L.
claims.adjustment: Age binary30-44 versus45-64, sex, BMI; fasting-time adjustment stated in article methods for glucose analyses.
claims.uncertainty: P values only for selected coefficients; no numeric SE/CI supplied in these rows.
claims.use: Adopt BMI location slope 0.0240*18=0.432 mg/dL per kg/m^2 and female-minus-male location contrast -0.2472*18=-4.4496 mg/dL. Extend to continuous age and the target age range by assumption. Do not adopt source intercept 4.2966 or binary age contrast as the target intercept or continuous-age slope.

claims.locator: Supplement Table S2, General population, Age+sex+BMI model
claims.reported: BMI beta0.0125 HbA1c percentage points per kg/m^2, P<0.0001; men versus women -0.0230 percentage points, P=0.2884; age30-44 versus45-64 -0.1120, P<0.0001; intercept5.1281.
claims.adjustment: Age binary30-44 versus45-64 and sex; fasting glucose is not a regressor.
claims.uncertainty: P values supplied; no numeric SE/CI for these coefficients in the selected table.
claims.use: Use 0.0125 as a reference age/sex-adjusted total BMI association, never label it glucose-adjusted. Algebraically subtract the assumed glucose pathway to set the direct conditional BMI coefficient0.009044. That decomposition is an explicit joint-law assumption. Source sex and intercept are not transferred numerically.

claims.locator: Statistical analysis paragraphs beginning 'Linear regression was applied'; Tables1,3,4; Results interaction paragraphs
claims.reported: Table1 means are age-adjusted predictive margins; Table3 R-squared for age+sex+BMI is0.1164 for HbA1c and0.1642 for fasting glucose in general population. Interactions occur in some population/sex subgroups.
claims.use: Do not equate predictive margins with raw means, R-squared with slopes, or nonsignificant interactions with absent interactions. Do not infer BMI SD from Table1 CIs or calibrate variance to R-squared. Heterogeneity limits transport.

source_selection.declined: No pooling of Finnish and migrant coefficients; no target HbA1c<6.5 restriction; no transfer of medication/register exclusions; no use of categorical anthropometry tables, which answer different estimands. Do not use the source discussion's unpublished 8% plasma/serum contrast as a universal correction.

source_selection.population: Taiwan Biobank, age30-70, n4748 after prior-diabetes exclusion; not all participants fasting; no target-equivalent glucose<126 eligibility.
source_selection.measurement_and_estimator: HbA1c percent; ordinary linear regression of HbA1c on age and sex, with additional univariate age/subgroup analyses. No survey weighting described for these regressions.

claims.reported: Age0.01401 percentage points/year (SE0.00081), male versus female0.08301 (SE0.01725), jointly adjusted only for age and sex. For HbA1c<6.5%, Table4 male SD0.32 and female SD0.34; these are subgroup SDs, not residual SDs.
claims.use: Context only: illustrates age/sex dependence, possible heterogeneity and HbA1c>=6.5 without prior diagnosis. Choose a small female contrast -0.04 as a transparent assumption; do not claim it is the source coefficient. Do not substitute0.01401 for a glucose/BMI-adjusted coefficient or transplant unselected high-HbA1c tails.

source_selection.declined: No direct numerical parameter adoption because fasting, glucose eligibility and adjustment differ; no requirement to force the reported subgroup interaction or sex reversal.

source_selection.population: Kerman Iran population cluster sample n604, age18-75. FBS<=126 subgroup n525 includes30 self-reported diabetes cases (Table1), unlike the requested prior-diagnosis exclusion. Single FBS-based grouping uses <=126 rather than strictly<126.
source_selection.measurement_and_estimator: Single enzyme-method FBS in mg/dL; HbA1c percent using Biosystem kit; unadjusted Pearson correlation and crude/age-sex-BMI-adjusted regression. No explicit survey-weighted correlation procedure described.

claims.locator: Results first paragraphs; Table1 T0001; Table2 T0002
claims.reported: FBS<=126 subgroup Pearson r0.23, n525, P<0.001; glucose91.2 SD12.4 mg/dL; HbA1c5.61 SD0.73%; BMI24.5 SD3.8. Table2 printed crude HbA1c-on-FBS beta0.13 and adjusted0.09; reverse crude beta0.38.
claims.uncertainty: P<0.001 for correlation and printed slopes; no coefficient SE/CI. SDs are participant dispersion, not estimate precision.
claims.use: Qualitative support for a nondeterministic, modest glucose-HbA1c relationship. The chosen conditional slope0.008 percentage points/(mg/dL), glucose SD10.5 and HbA1c SD0.31 are assumptions, not source estimates.
claims.decline_reason: Crude slope implied by Pearson r and reported SDs is0.23*0.73/12.4=0.013540322580645161, not the printed0.13 on stated mg/dL scale. A missing scaling factor may explain it, but is not silently repaired. Also unadjusted correlation cannot identify the needed conditional slope and treated/diagnosed cases differ. Decline direct regression coefficient and exact dispersion transfer.

overlap: Main text, XML, metadata and supplementary extraction formats for each PMC item describe the same study, not replicate evidence. FOS cross-sectional and longitudinal results overlap participants; only the NHANES adjusted age association is used. The Taiwan article cites PMC2551641, which is not an additional independent confirmation. No formal evidence pooling or independence-weighted meta-analysis is performed.

assumptions.statement: Selected US and Finnish parameters transfer unchanged as provisional location relationships to the specified Mexican analytical design. This is not established by the admitted evidence. Source weighting, assay, fasting-duration, HbA1c selection, age range, ancestry and unmeasured exclusions differ.

BMI follows an age/sex-independent truncated lognormal with untruncated mean28.01, logSD0.20 and open support12-65. The untruncated SD5.65849 is a consequence of this assumed shape. Source age-pattern text does not prove independence; sex independence is a simplification. Rare more extreme BMI values are outside the chosen law.

Conditional glucose location96 at age50, male, BMI28; age slope0.16; residual SD10.5; normal residual law restricted to actual eligibility0<G<126. Treat source regression coefficients as pre-truncation location slopes, not guaranteed fitted post-truncation slopes. No selection-induced change in BMI distribution is reconstructed because the law directly describes the selected population.
Use conventional rounded18.0 mg/dL per mmol/L for glucose; not an assay/serum-plasma calibration.

Choose H glucose coefficient0.008 and subtract its product with the source-inspired G-BMI coefficient from the age/sex-adjusted BMI coefficient0.0125 to define H's conditional BMI coefficient. This combines nonidentical source populations plus an assumed conditional association. Q3 and the Q2/Q3 difference are assumption-dependent; no causal interpretation, empirical target result or exact truncation-invariant equality is claimed.

H reference location5.38 at age50,male,BMI28,G95; female contrast-0.04; residual SD0.31+0.001*(age-50); independent normal conditional residual; broad open support2-12. These fix individual dispersion, sex dependence, location and tails without fitting source SEs or target results. Anemia and medication are not excluded or individually modeled.

Centers50years,28kg/m^2,95mg/dL define intercepts only and differ harmlessly from requested analysis centers. Balanced within-cell integer ages are an analytical-design assumption. Additive location laws and no interactions simplify inconsistent source subgroup patterns.

Unrepresented diagnosis, fasting records, measurement consistency and documented pregnancy/lactation routing are assumed as cohort membership, not verified by fictional row values. No verified medication or anemia exclusion is asserted.
